title: Rav Huna bar Ada

paragraphs: According to the reading in Dikdukei Soferim, Rav Huna bar Ada is mentioned in Berakhot 62b, speaking in the name of Rav Sama son of Rav Mari. Hyman gives the received reading as Rav Chana bar Ada.

notes.text: The supplied text has רב נא בר אדא, Rav Na bar Ada. The William Davidson digital Berakhot 62b paragraph has רב חנא בר אדא, Rav Chana bar Ada, reporting Rav Sama son of Rav Mari. Whether the missing ח belongs to the supplied transcription or Hyman’s printing remains unestablished; no printed-page proof is claimed.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 347) reads Rav Chana bar Ada, with the letter missing from the supplied transcription. Dikdukei Soferim on Berakhot, p. 364, prints Chana in the received-text column and Huna in the manuscript column. Both readings retain the attribution to Rav Sama son of Rav Mari in the discussion of a shortcut through the Temple Mount.
